document.title: In Bilateral Focussed on Afghanistan, GOP Reviews Pak/Iran Effort; A/S Inderfurth Expresses U.S. Concerns About the Taliban (Islama 05535)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Pakistan: "The Taliban's Godfather"?
document.note: [Confidential] A/S Karl Inderfurth meets Pakistani Foreign Minister Shamshad Ahmed on joint Pakistan/Iran talks and Pakistan's role. Ahmed denies providing anything but oil and wheat to the Taliban and says similar help went to the northern factions.

events.description: Inderfurth met Foreign Secretary Shamshad Ahmad on Afghanistan.
Taliban and Masood exchanged prisoners (300 each; embassy estimate ~140 total).
Sharif met Khatami at ECO summit, starting Pak/Iran initiative.
Kharazi visited Islamabad; Kanju team toured Afghanistan.
Six-plus-two meeting discussed the Pak/Iran effort.
Richardson-brokered face-to-face Taliban talks; Taliban agreed no new offensives.
Sharif met Khatami at the ECO summit in Almaty, launching the Pak/Iran joint Afghanistan peace initiative.
Iranian FM Kharazi visited Islamabad at Sharif's invitation; agreed on coordinated visits to Afghanistan.
Pakistani team led by Siddique Kanju held talks in north and south Afghanistan and provided humanitarian aid to Badakhshan earthquake victims.
Earthquake in Badakhshan.
Taliban and Masood's Jamiat-i-Islami each released prisoners to the other side (reported 300 each; embassy sources say ~140 total).
Inderfurth met Foreign Secretary Shamshad Ahmad in Islamabad on Afghanistan; Ahmad urged U.S. to support vacating Afghan UN seat; Inderfurth declined.
Richardson-brokered face-to-face talks with Taliban, who agreed not to launch new military offensives.
Taliban ordered NGOs to relocate and girls' home-based schools to close.
Murshed and Borujerdi expected to make a joint visit to Kandahar and Mazar-i-Sharif soon.
Six-Plus-Two meeting discussed the Pakistan-Iran joint initiative.
Masood and Taliban informally exchanged 300 prisoners each.
Taliban advanced into Faryab, about 30 km from Maimana; Dostam ousted from Shibarghan.
European Commission decided to suspend assistance to Kabul after Taliban NGO relocation order.
Pakistani MFA gave Inderfurth talking points; 'Afghan dialogue' meeting criticized in Bonn.
Taliban education minister Nomani visiting US to discuss funding for schools.
Fighting among Northern Alliance groups last month.

U.S. Embassy Islamabad transmits a cable (Islama 05535, section 5 of 5) to the State Department reporting a bilateral meeting focused on Afghanistan. The Government of Pakistan reviewed the Pak/Iran effort, and A/S Inderfurth expressed U.S. concerns about the Taliban. The closing text stresses reconstruction and rehabilitation as an inducement to Afghan groups to accelerate the peace process.

relationships.quote: A/S INDERFURTH EXPRESSES U.S. CONCERNS ABOUT THE TALIBAN

key_claims: Pakistan's MFA talking points were described by the embassy as basically pro-Taliban.
Pakistan denied giving the Taliban anything but oil and wheat, and claimed equal aid went to the northern factions.
Pakistan urged vacating the Afghan UN seat; the U.S. refused given Taliban NGO and girls' school policies.
The U.S. suggested Pakistan and Iran supply different Afghan factions and that this should be discussed.
The Taliban advanced into Faryab while Pakistan and Iran pursued a joint peace initiative.
